lessons.code:
# Class · Python with real data
import pandas as pd

sales = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
mean = sales["amount"].mean()
print(f"Mean: {mean:.2f} €")
# → Mean: 48.73 €

# Class · Big Data with PySpark
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

df = spark.read.parquet("sales/")
(df.groupBy("country")
   .agg(F.sum("amount"))
   .show())
# → millions of rows, in parallel

# Class · AI: which model?
sensitive_data = True
if sensitive_data:
    option = "open model, run locally"
else:
    option = "a provider's API"
print(option)
# → open model, run locally

# Class · Free AI, run locally
# First: ollama pull llama3.2
import ollama

r = ollama.generate(model="llama3.2",
    prompt="What is a DataFrame?")
print(r["response"])
# → your own model, for free

-- Class · Analytical SQL
SELECT country, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM sales
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 5;
-- → the 5 best-selling markets

about.title: Learning is still a human thing
about.p1: IsAcademy was born from a simple idea: in an increasingly artificial world, real learning needs a person who listens, explains and challenges you.
about.p2: It was founded by Ismael Sarmiento, a Lead Data Engineer specialised in data governance and passionate about teaching, with over 10 years working in the tech industry and training professionals. We bring what companies actually do into every class, with patience, a personal approach and a plan tailored to each student.
about.p3: We use AI as a tool, never as a shortcut: we want you to understand what you do and to solve problems on your own.
about.role: Founder and tutor · Lead Data Engineer

method.title: Theory you understand, practice you apply

facts: Python is named after the comedy group Monty Python, not the snake.
The most famous computer “bug” was a real moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer, in 1947.
SQL was born at IBM in the 1970s under the name SEQUEL.
John McCarthy coined the term “Artificial Intelligence” in 1955, in the proposal for the Dartmouth conference held in 1956.
In the 19th century Ada Lovelace wrote what is considered the first algorithm intended for a machine.
Apache Spark started in 2009 as a research project at the University of California, Berkeley.
Hadoop is named after the toy elephant of one of its creators' son.
In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov.
In 2016, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol, one of the best Go players in the world.
Type “import this” in Python and you get the Zen of Python: 19 principles for writing good code.
The word “algorithm” comes from the name of the 9th-century Persian mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
In 1950 Alan Turing proposed the “imitation game”, now the Turing test: can a machine pass as human in a conversation?
A byte has 8 bits, enough to represent 256 different values.
The relational model behind SQL databases was proposed by Edgar F. Codd in 1970.
The pandas library takes its name from “panel data”, a data type used in econometrics.
Grace Hopper built one of the first compilers and championed programming with words instead of numbers.
Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
Arthur Samuel popularised the term “machine learning” in 1959 with a program that learned to play checkers.
The perceptron, one of the first artificial neural networks, dates from 1958.
Much of a data scientist's work is cleaning and preparing data, not training models.

IsAcademy was founded by Ismael Sarmiento, a Lead Data Engineer specialised in data governance and passionate about teaching, with over 10 years working in the tech industry and training professionals. His students rate him 5 ★.
We teach Python, object-oriented programming, SQL, data analytics, Big Data with Spark, Data Engineering and Artificial Intelligence. We also guide theses and careers.

In Python we start from your level: syntax and logic, functions and good practices, and automation and working with data. Every concept is learned by writing code, with your own project that grows with you.
In SQL we cover queries, JOINs and aggregations, data modelling and analytical queries, always on realistic databases and business questions.
In AI we cover machine learning fundamentals, generative AI and language models, and how to use AI with judgement. Just enough theory not to treat it as a black box, applied to practical cases.

Yes, you can use AI for free: with open models running on your own computer (for example with Ollama or Hugging Face). It's one of the mini-lessons at the top of the page, and we go deep into it in our AI classes.
It depends on the task, the privacy of your data and your budget. With sensitive data an open local model is usually better; otherwise an API can be more convenient. We decide together for your case.
In Big Data we cover distributed processing, Apache Spark and PySpark, and cloud data platforms, with real volumes to understand when it's needed.
In Data Engineering we build a complete pipeline step by step: ETL/ELT design, orchestration with tools like Airflow, and data quality and governance.
In data analytics we work on cleaning and analysis with pandas, clear visualisation and storytelling with data, starting from real questions.
In object-oriented programming we cover classes, inheritance and composition, design principles and patterns, and refactoring with tests.
We guide you from idea to defence: choosing the topic, guidance and review of the technical work, write-up review and defence rehearsal. The work is yours; the method and the confidence, ours.
In career guidance we help with a roadmap for your profile, your CV, portfolio and LinkedIn, and technical interview preparation, from someone who works in the industry.
We combine clear explanations, practice with real cases and challenges with visible progress. First a free assessment of your case, then a plan for you, guided practice and a real project.
Every two weeks we open a free online classroom to answer questions live about Python, SQL, data or AI. Anyone can join: message us through the form and we'll let you know about the next one.
